title: You know what time it is... STORY TIME
summary: Three-hour story-time stream opening with a quick Q&A (weighted pull-up numbers, decline bench, training schedule, sleep, gym prices) followed by long life stories: his one disastrous weed experience, airport security nightmares and the Newark trip that ended with him being fired, failures with women and a false accusation, a sociopathic bully, his violent Paris 'prison school', getting harassed out of his university gym (which led to his first home gym and the channel), and his fight with the French school system. He ends with channel plans for 2025.
claims: Matt Wenning's warm-up system with lots of reps is not useful for hypertrophy and wastes energy
He does weighted chin-ups for sets of 8 with 60 lb, holding a dumbbell between his feet instead of using a dip belt because it is more practical
His regular-grip weighted pull-ups are sets of 3-5 reps with 115 lb (two plates and some change)
He no longer uses the Slingshot bench aid and is selling it
If pressing gives you pain near the armpit, try pressing with the elbows tucked closer to the body
Taking a walk every day regardless of weather, even in a blizzard, helps mental health and seasonal depression
If you have little time to read, read first thing in the morning and right before bed
Hypertrophy training increases how much sleep you need because the nervous system requires more rest
Training right before bed is a bad idea because it revs you up too much; night work shifts are fine
He high-bar squats only 3-5 times a year (last time about four plates) and enjoys seeing how much it has improved without training it; he does the same with bench
Birthdays, New Year and Christmas are regular days for him; he does not celebrate them
French gym-goers are ruder than Americans, reserving machines; the idea that Americans are aggressive is European cope
A $100/month gym is expensive; look for an uncrowded mom-and-pop gym around $40-50; his own pro bodybuilding gym with IFBB pros is nearly empty
He is agnostic but spiritual, influenced by Catholicism, Sunni Islam and lessons from nature
His week: three home-gym sessions, two commercial-gym sessions (limited by gas prices) and two backyard weighted-carry sessions
He no longer cares about views and would restart from 100 subscribers if the channel were taken down
Daily foam rolling is fine, a bit like rice-bucket training, as long as you don't go too hard
He has taken cold showers for seven years; it is a habit he thinks is good, especially in a cold climate
He was laid off after six years at a large company despite two bachelor's degrees and a master's, which pushed him to work for himself
He does not monetize his YouTube channel
He is straight edge: no alcohol and no drugs of any kind, not just no steroids
His one heavy weed experience (a thumb-thick pure joint) wiped his short-term memory for hours and he wandered Paris all night; he never smoked heavily again for fear of permanent brain damage
High on weed he believed he could pump his biceps and quads just by thinking about them while walking
At the Newark airport he sprinted all-out for the first time in five years at about 220 lb (last time he was around 170 lb) and his joints creaked
Some men only respect strength: a sadistic childhood bully treated him as a friend once he had grown a foot and become muscular
He beat bullying by learning from a friend that you must appear crazy and retaliate instantly whenever someone messes with you
Being surrounded by people better than you raises your level far more than being the best among weak peers
Reading philosophy concepts for 10 minutes every night all year let him ace a surprise test the rest of the class failed
Swimming talent he had as a pre-puberty national-level swimmer vanished after five years without training, humbling him at a school swim exam
University gym staff vacuumed between his legs while he squatted about 300 lb and mopped with bleach while people trained
He used Tiger Balm on his tendons to warm them because his tendons were in bad shape
A friend benched 225 lb for 4 cheat reps with his butt off the bench and never added a rep or pound in four years, ignoring advice
Gym staff told him to be quieter after an overhead press with 175 lb
Fear of being banned by a hostile gym staffer motivated him to build his first home gym (a planned 16x8 ft space with a self-made platform), which led to the channel
The steroid users he befriended at the university gym were all insane and in pain, and all died during his stay, which convinced him never to use
One gym bro cruised on tren permanently, was mentally wrecked, and still struggled to bench three plates
Storytelling is less about the stories themselves than how you tell them
He is cutting stream frequency in early 2025 to prioritize videos while working 60-80 hour weeks
He left French education for America because an American degree is more valuable
Upcoming content: a hypertrophy log, a long insult video and free programs
Today's session: squats and reverse lunges
exercises: dumbbell held between the feet instead of a belt
normal pull-up grip, heavy low reps
tested a few times a year
